Cautiously supportive tone. The decision to hold the federal funds rate at 2.25–2.50% while emphasizing “patience” is consistent with Taylor-rule style behavior that responds to softer activity and inflation near, but slightly below, the 2% goal (the Fed’s behavior often resembles a Taylor rule). Low market-based inflation compensation points to subdued expected inflation and/or lower inflation risk premia, in line with bond-pricing evidence that nominal–indexed spreads embed expectations and risk premiums. With expectations relatively anchored, a hybrid Phillips curve (Gali–Gertler) implies muted inflation pressure despite a tight labor market, which supports waiting. The communication also aligns with inflation-forecast targeting (Svensson; Svensson and Woodford), and New Keynesian guidance (Christiano–Eichenbaum–Evans; Woodford) to balance output and inflation gaps rather than tighten preemptively. Overall, strong labor data offset slower spending and investment and declining headline inflation (energy-driven), yielding a cautious-but-constructive macro assessment.
